explicacion.en: Le is usted, so the verb must also be the usted form: beba. Bebas goes with te.

titulo.en: Recommending: recomendar + que + subjunctive

texto.en: To tell someone what you think they should do, Spanish uses recomendar (to recommend) + que + the present subjunctive: Te recomiendo que corras. English can say “I recommend you run” without “that”; Spanish needs que before the second verb: Te recomiendo que corras, not Te recomiendo corras. The two verbs have different subjects: yo recomiendo, tú corres. Recomendar changes e to ie (recomiendo, recomiendas, recomienda, recomendamos, recomiendan). You can also use aconsejar (to advise) in the same way: Te aconsejo que bebas agua. Review of the subjunctive: -ar verbs take the endings -e, -es, -e, -emos, -en; -er and -ir verbs take -a, -as, -a, -amos, -an. Stem changes stay (empezar: empieces; dormir: duermas), and some verbs are irregular (hacer: hagas; ir: vayas).

titulo.en: Tú or usted

texto.en: With a friend (tú) use te and the tú form of the subjunctive: Te recomiendo que empieces. With usted use le and the usted form, which is the same as the él/ella form: Le recomiendo que empiece. Compare: tú → que bebas; usted → que beba. The pronoun te/le tells you who receives the advice, so you can also talk about a third person: Daniela le recomienda a Emma que descanse. In the dialogue, Daniela and Emma use tú, while the Entrenador (a new instructor she has just met) and Emma use usted. A softer way to give advice without que is deberías + infinitive: Deberías ir poco a poco (review).

contexto.en: A gym in La Mariscal, in the afternoon. Emma wants to run a five-kilometer race in three months. Daniela, who has been running for two years, gives her tips; Emma and Daniela use tú. Then Emma meets the Entrenador, a new instructor at the gym who does not know her yet, and he gives advice; he and Emma use usted because they have just met.

dialogo.texto: Hola, Daniela. Quiero correr una carrera de cinco kilómetros dentro de tres meses, pero no sé cómo empezar.

traduccion.en: Hi, Daniela. I want to run a five-kilometer race in three months, but I don't know how to start.

dialogo.texto: ¡Qué bien, Emma! Yo corro desde hace dos años. Te recomiendo que empieces despacio. Es mejor ir poco a poco.

traduccion.en: How great, Emma! I've been running for two years. I recommend that you start slowly. It's better to go little by little.

dialogo.texto: ¿Cuánto tiempo corro al principio?

traduccion.en: How long do I run at the beginning?

dialogo.texto: Te recomiendo que corras quince minutos, tres veces por semana. También te recomiendo que compres zapatillas nuevas y que bebas agua.

traduccion.en: I recommend that you run fifteen minutes, three times a week. I also recommend that you buy new sneakers and drink water.

dialogo.texto: Buena idea. Mis zapatillas son muy viejas. Gracias, Daniela. Eres una buena amiga.

traduccion.en: Good idea. My sneakers are very old. Thanks, Daniela. You are a good friend.

dialogo.texto: De nada. Yo siempre corro por la mañana, pero tú puedes correr por la tarde.

traduccion.en: You're welcome. I always run in the morning, but you can run in the afternoon.

dialogo.texto: Mira, allí está el instructor nuevo. Él sabe mucho de resistencia.

traduccion.en: Look, the new instructor is over there. He knows a lot about stamina.

dialogo.texto: Buenas tardes. Me llamo Emma. Quiero empezar a correr. ¿Qué me recomienda?

traduccion.en: Good afternoon. My name is Emma. I want to start running. What do you recommend? (usted)

dialogo.texto: Mucho gusto, Emma. Le recomiendo que haga cinco minutos de calentamiento antes de correr y estiramientos después.

traduccion.en: Nice to meet you, Emma. I recommend that you do five minutes of warm-up before running and stretches afterward.

dialogo.texto: ¿Y si siento cansancio?

traduccion.en: And if I feel tired?

dialogo.texto: Es normal al principio. Le recomiendo que descanse un día después de cada carrera.

traduccion.en: That's normal at the beginning. I recommend that you rest one day after each run.

dialogo.texto: Muchas gracias. Voy a empezar el lunes. Mi meta es correr los cinco kilómetros.

traduccion.en: Thank you very much. I'm going to start on Monday. My goal is to run the five kilometers.

dialogo.texto: ¡Perfecto!

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Es bueno que usas hilo dental.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Es bueno que uses hilo dental.

explicacion.en: After es bueno que, Spanish needs the subjunctive: uses. English speakers often keep the present indicative (usas) because English has no change after “It's good that you use…”.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Es importante que cepillarse los dientes.

explicacion.en: After que there must be a conjugated verb with its own subject: Es importante que te cepilles. For general advice, drop que and use the infinitive: Es importante cepillarse.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Es mejor que se cepillas después de comer.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Es mejor que se cepille después de comer.

explicacion.en: Se goes with the usted form, so the verb must be cepille. Cepillas goes with te.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Es bueno para que te cepilles.

explicacion.en: English says “It's good for you to brush”, but Spanish does not use para here: es bueno que + subjunctive.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Es malo que comes tantos dulces.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Es malo que comas tantos dulces.

explicacion.en: Es malo que needs the subjunctive: comas. Comes is the present indicative.

titulo.en: Opinions: es bueno / es mejor / es malo / es importante + que

texto.en: To say what is good, better, bad or important for a specific person, Spanish uses es bueno, es mejor, es malo or es importante + que + the present subjunctive: Es bueno que te cepilles los dientes. The two parts have different subjects (“it” and tú), and the phrase gives an opinion, not a fact, so the verb after que goes in the subjunctive. With usted: Es mejor que se cepille después de cada comida. You already know the same pattern from recomendar and from es necesario que: Es necesario que tenga su pasaporte. The forms are the ones you already know from earlier lessons (uses, comas, vayas, tengas…).

titulo.en: General advice or advice for one person

texto.en: If the advice is for everyone, Spanish uses es + adjective + infinitive: Es importante cepillarse los dientes (It is important to brush your teeth). If you are talking to a concrete person, use que + subjunctive: Es importante que te cepilles los dientes (It is important that you brush your teeth). Compare: general → Es mejor usar hilo dental; to a person → Es mejor que uses hilo dental. Cepillarse is reflexive, so the pronoun changes with the subject: me cepille, te cepilles, se cepille, nos cepillemos, se cepillen. Remember that Spanish uses the article with parts of the body: los dientes, not “your teeth”.

contexto.en: A dentist's office in La Mariscal, in the morning. Emma has a checkup. The Dentista and Emma use usted. The Dentista says there are no cavities but the gums are a little swollen, and gives advice.

explicacion.en: Yo que tú is followed by the conditional, not by the present. English says “If I were you, I'd go”, and the Spanish “I'd go” is iría.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Yo que tú descansarías.

explicacion.en: The one speaking is yo, so the verb is the yo form: descansaría. The -ías ending (descansarías) is for tú and would mean “you would rest”.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Yo que tu iría al médico.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Yo que tú iría al médico.

explicacion.en: Tú (you) needs its accent. Without it, tu means “your”.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Yo en tu lugar hacería ejercicio.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Yo en tu lugar haría ejercicio.

explicacion.en: Hacer is irregular in the conditional: the stem is har-, so it is haría, not hacería.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Yo en tu lugar iré al médico.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Yo en tu lugar iría al médico.

explicacion.en: Iré is the future (I will go). To say what you would do in the other person's place, use the conditional: iría.

titulo.en: Putting yourself in the other person's place

texto.en: To give advice by imagining yourself in the other person's situation, Spanish uses yo que tú or yo en tu lugar + the conditional: Yo que tú iría al médico (If I were you, I'd go to the doctor). English says “If I were you…”, but Spanish does not use a subjunctive here: after the expression comes the conditional. The conditional is formed with the infinitive + -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -ían: descansar → descansaría, dormir → dormiría, ir → iría. A few verbs are irregular: hacer → haría, decir → diría. The verb is in the yo form because the speaker is “I”: Yo en tu lugar descansaría. The words yo and tú stay in the expression; they are part of it.

titulo.en: Tú or usted

texto.en: With a friend (tú): yo que tú / yo en tu lugar. With usted: yo que usted / yo en su lugar. In the dialogue Emma and Dr. Mena use usted, so the doctor says Yo en su lugar descansaría. Do not write tu without an accent: in yo que tú, the tú has an accent because it is the pronoun “you”. To say what you would not do, put no before the conditional: Yo que usted no correría. Review: to say that something hurts, use doler: Me duele la rodilla (my knee hurts).

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Dejé correr.

explicacion.en: English says “I stopped running” with no small word, but Spanish needs de after dejar when you stop doing something: dejar de + infinitive.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Dejé de corriendo.

explicacion.en: After a preposition (de) Spanish uses the infinitive, not the gerund. English “stopped running” is not translated word for word.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Sigo correr.

explicacion.en: Seguir + gerund means to keep doing something: sigo corriendo. The infinitive does not work after seguir in this meaning.

explicacion.en: To say “again”, Spanish uses volver a + infinitive. The small word a cannot be dropped.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Volví de correr.

explicacion.en: Volví de correr would mean “I came back from running”. To say you did it again, use volver a: volví a correr.

titulo.en: Dejar de, seguir and volver a

texto.en: Three structures describe how habits change. Dejar de + infinitive means to stop doing something: Dejé de tomar café (I stopped drinking coffee). Seguir + gerund means to keep doing something: Sigo corriendo (I keep running). Volver a + infinitive means to do something again: Volví a nadar (I swam again, I went back to swimming). In English the meaning is built with “stop”, “keep” and “again”; in Spanish the small words de and a are required. Do not mix the forms: after dejar de and volver a use the infinitive, and after seguir use the gerund (-ando, -iendo). Review of the gerund: correr → corriendo, estudiar → estudiando, hacer → haciendo. With seguir the pronoun can attach to the gerund: sigue levantándose (an accent mark appears).

titulo.en: Using them with time and frequency

texto.en: These expressions combine with markers of time and frequency you already know: todos los días, tres veces por semana, por la noche. They also tell a story in time: Dejé de correr (a past moment), pero volví a nadar (and I came back), y sigo haciendo estiramientos (and I still do them). Note the difference: dejé de correr = I stopped running; dejé corriendo would mean I left something running (for example, the water). Retomar is a one-word way to say volver a hacer something: retomé la natación.

titulo.en: para + infinitive or para que + subjunctive

texto.en: Para says what something is for. When the subject is the same in both parts, use para + infinitive: Hago ejercicio para estar bien (I exercise to be well: the same person exercises and is well). When the subject changes, use para que + subjunctive: Te doy esta hoja para que hagas los ejercicios (I give you the sheet so that you do the exercises: yo give, tú do). Para que is always followed by the subjunctive, and it is the Spanish way to say “so that” or “in order that”. English often says “to”, but Spanish cannot use para + infinitive when there is a second person: say Te lo explico para que entiendas, not Te lo explico para entender (that would mean I explain it in order to understand).

titulo.en: With recommendations and with usted

texto.en: You can add para que to a recommendation: Descanse para que la rodilla mejore (Rest so that your knee gets better). The knee is a different subject from the person who rests, so you need para que. With usted the subjunctive is the él/ella form: Le doy esta crema para que le baje la inflamación. Note the reflexive verb: la rodilla se recupere (the knee recovers). The other forms are in the table: with ustedes the subjunctive ends in -en.

consigna.en: Writing task (at least 14 words, not scored): explain to Daniela why you follow Dr. Mena's instructions, using “para” and “para que”. Compare with the model.

feedback.en: Model: Descanso dos semanas para que la rodilla se recupere. Hago estiramientos para estar bien y la doctora me da ejercicios para que pueda correr la carrera.
